tonight.headline: Sadiq's Friday decides the tight end; the flex is still a point off
body: The bad news is unchanged: Kenyon Sadiq, your only tight end, was limited Wednesday and Thursday with his back, and no bench player can cover him. This afternoon's practice is his last before a designation. ESPN has you at 123.3 against Team 13's 96.6, 64%, up from 55% yesterday because their side is breaking.

One thing to do before Sunday 07:30: the flex still has Tuten where the projection prefers Downs by a point. It's a coin flip, so take the projection (card 1). If Sadiq is ruled out, Mark Andrews is still a free agent and practised fully both days.

case.label: Their side
case.body: Team 13 start DeVonta Smith, who hasn't practised and isn't expected to play: ESPN's Tim McManus has the Eagles preparing without him (NBC 1 Oct), and he projects 0.0. Their RB2 Rachaad White (shoulder) missed Wednesday and Thursday (SI 2 Oct). DJ Moore on their bench was limited with a shoulder. Josh Allen isn't on Buffalo's report; Lamar Jackson, benched behind him, was full Thursday.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Team 13 moving DJ Moore and Blake Corum into the lineup for Smith and White: that's about 20 projected points back and the gap narrows to roughly six.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Before Sun 07:30 Mexico City (Downs locks in London)
doFirst.title: Put Downs back in the flex over Tuten
doFirst.subtitle: 13.7 to 12.7. Carried for a third run and still not done. A coin flip, so it goes to the projection — and no thesis.

case.label: The rule
case.body: lineup_check.py: 'start Josh Downs 13.7 over Bhayshul Tuten 12.7 — COIN FLIP, take the projection.' Neither has news ESPN hasn't priced: Downs isn't on the Colts' Wednesday or Thursday report (Colts.com 1 Oct) and Tuten isn't on Jacksonville's (Bengals.com 1 Oct).

case.label: The player
case.body: Downs drew 11 targets in Week 3, a third of Indianapolis' (archive), with Pierce on IR. Keenan Allen was limited again Thursday with a groin issue that RotoWire calls partly rest. Washington have allowed the most points to receivers (footballdb, standard scoring).

case.label: The timing cost
case.body: Downs locks at 07:30 in London, Tuten at 11:00. Putting Downs in the flex gives up a little late flexibility, but nothing on this roster is waiting on a later inactive except Sadiq, and only a tight end covers him.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Tuten outscores Downs. It's a coin flip: this is the expected-value call, not a prediction, and it gets no decision-log entry.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only · if Sadiq is ruled out Friday or inactive at Sun 09:30 Mexico City; both lock at 11:00
doFirst.title: If Sadiq sits: add Mark Andrews, drop Carnell Tate
doFirst.subtitle: Carried. Andrews is still a free agent, so it's an add with no priority cost.

case.label: The injury
case.body: Sadiq hurt his back on a diving touchdown catch in Week 3 and has been limited Wednesday and Thursday (NewYorkJets.com; RotoWire; NBC, 1 Oct). Friday is his last chance to upgrade. No coach has spoken to his availability. Mason Taylor (thumb) hasn't practised. ESPN: QUESTIONABLE at 9.9.

case.label: The fallback
case.body: Andrews projects 10.1 at home to Tennessee and was a full participant Wednesday and Thursday with a hand listing; he runs a route on 65.6% of dropbacks with 23.7% of the targets (FantasyPros 1 Oct). Against that, Zay Flowers had his first full practice since before Week 1, which is likelier to shrink Andrews' share than grow it. He's a FREEAGENT in this snapshot: an add, not a claim, and anyone else can make it first.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Carnell Tate, the fifth receiver and not on the screen's exposure list. Kamara and Gordon are on it, and Golden and Downs both project above him, so none of them is the drop.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: It fires and Andrews scores less than the best free tight end that week (Hunter Henry, Loveland).

whatWentWrong.title: The flex has sat a point below the projection since Wednesday night
whatWentWrong.lead: Downs went into the flex at 14:10 Wednesday and back out for Tuten at 21:31 that night, Mexico City time. Three briefs later it hasn't moved.

case.label: Why it matters
case.body: Section 0 of the strategy: every Week 1–2 loss was winnable with the roster owned, and the most expensive mistake was overriding the projection. A one-point flip isn't a disaster; the habit is.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: News ESPN hasn't priced about Downs or Tuten. I found none: both are off Thursday's reports.

worthALook.name: Bills D/ST
worthALook.lead: The D/ST comparison: the Bills are free at 8.0, the Ravens project 7.3. Hold.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: Bills 8.0 at home to New England, the wire's biggest riser at +7.98. Ravens 7.3 at home to a Titans team with Tony Pollard back to a full practice and a quarterback at the bottom of the league in yards per attempt (Titans.com; FantasyPros 1 Oct), with Trey Hendrickson missing two practices (Ravens.com). The Steelers, 8.2 yesterday, played Thursday and scored 6.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: The gap is 0.7, and the D/ST seat changed hands on Wednesday. The churn rule closes it.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Hendrickson ruled out and the Ravens' number falling a point below a free defence that hasn't kicked off.

worthALook.name: Ka'imi Fairbairn
worthALook.lead: The kicker comparison: 0.1 better than Myers and now a free agent. Hold.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: Fairbairn 9.8, Myers 9.7. He cleared waivers and costs no priority now, but the kicker seat changed hands on Wednesday and a tenth of a point isn't a reason to change it again.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Myers appearing on Seattle's report.

doNotChase.name: Kendre Miller
doNotChase.lead: The wire's biggest running-back riser, and the other half of a backfield you already own.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Travis Etienne went on IR for at least four weeks, and Kellen Moore said 'Alvin and Kendre will handle that load really well' (CBS 1 Oct). Yahoo projects Miller for early-down work; that's an analyst, not the coach.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 4 carries and 3 targets for 3.9 points in Week 3 (archive), 15 touches all season. You own Kamara, the lead half, who projects 10.6 to Miller's 8.8 and still sits on your bench.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Miller out-touching Kamara on Monday night: then Kamara is the problem to solve, not a reason to own both.

doNotChase.name: Keenan Allen
doNotChase.lead: Still rising, and still the same role reason you already own in Downs.

case.label: The rise
case.body: 27% of Indianapolis targets in Week 3 with Pierce on IR (archive). Limited Wednesday and Thursday with a groin; severity 'not yet known' (Yahoo), partly rest (RotoWire 1 Oct).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Downs, yours, drew 11 targets to Allen's 9 in Week 3 (archive) from the same vacancy. Doubling up on one team's opening buys nothing.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Downs hurt.

doNotChase.name: Jaylen Wright
doNotChase.lead: Upgraded to a full practice Thursday; he's splitting the backfield you spent priority on.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Limited Wednesday with the foot, full Thursday (FantasyPros; NBC; RotoWire; CBS, 1 Oct). Fowler expects him back this week and sharing the load with Gordon (ESPN via Yahoo 30 Sep).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: He'd be a fifth back on a roster that starts two, at Minnesota (4th-fewest to RBs, footballdb). A free agent, but a roster seat is still a cost. ESPN: 7.5 to Gordon's 9.0.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Wright takes over Miami outright (Gordon under 8 touches) — then Gordon is the problem to solve, not a reason to own both.

waiverAnalysis.summary: Nothing on the wire beats this roster on usage, from three weeks of data, which is still thin. The only wire need is the Sadiq fallback, an injury plan rather than a usage gap.
